question.problem:
A particle’s acceleration in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ is given by the function $a(t)=\sqrt{t},$ where $t$ is the time in seconds.  

Find the average acceleration ${a}_{\text{avg}}$ of the particle on the interval $[1,4].$ Do not round your answer.

${a}_{\text{avg}}=$ 
{{field-1}}
${\text{m/s}}^{2}$
question.worked_solution:
To calculate the average value of the acceleration on $[{t}_{1},{t}_{2}],$ we use the average value formula

$$
{a}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{{t}_{2}-{t}_{1}}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}a(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{4-1}{\int }_{1}^{4}\sqrt{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{(\frac{2}{3}{t}^{3/2})|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(\frac{2}{3}\cdot 8)-(\frac{2}{3}\cdot 1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{16}{3}-\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{14}{3}) \\  & =\frac{14}{9}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average acceleration is $\frac{14}{9}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$
